name: 2024 Panel platform/document/AI concealment methods

attribution.legal_posture: UN Panel reporting; some claims reproduce Member State information and remain outside criminal adjudication.

caveats: A platform assessment that most skilled freelance crypto profiles were fake was an opinion and is rejected as too broad for publication.
AI use, remote work, crypto work, VPN use and one inconsistent profile are contextual signals; attribution requires a broader source-backed pattern.

statements: The Panel compiled reports of falsified resumes, inconsistent cross-platform identities, purchased or borrowed high-reputation accounts, photo-realistic identity-document and supporting-document generators, account-resale services, and proxy email/SMS services.

DPRK IT workers reportedly used generative AI for profile images, profile text and coding/interview answers; workers increasingly approached cryptocurrency companies and community chats directly when major platforms tightened controls.
Reports also described seeking web3, blockchain, smart-contract and cryptocurrency work and potentially exploiting or inserting vulnerabilities.

sources.support: Supports the platform migration, document/account services, proxy communications, generative-AI and crypto-project methods
sources.locator: PDF pp. 50-51, paras. 151-153; PDF pp. 354-360, annex 64
